#FundraiseAlert! 

C-CAMP-supported bioLOCKEY Healthworks gets support from Gates Foundation India to advance its diagnostic solutions for early detection of cervical cancer risk and preeclampsia, a serious pregnancy complication.

🔗https://lnkd.in/p/gRcCpAAx 

Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in India, while preeclampsia is the third leading cause of maternal mortality in India.

Underserved women in India carry a high burden of both health challenges.

Biolockey's advanced diagnostic solutions, driven by their proprietary point-of-care nanobody-based reagents innovation platform, will be a huge step towards affordable and accessible disease detection in low-resource settings. 

Biolockey is supported through the C-CAMP - Startup India SISFS scheme and our bioincubation programmes. 

#CCAMP #WomenHealth

Dr Jitendra Singh | Taslimarif Saiyed, PhD | Piyush Goyal | Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India | NITI Aayog | Department of Biotechnology | Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) |  Atal Innovation Mission Official | Priyank M Kharge | IT BT Department, Karnataka |  Startup Karnataka | India-DST | Rajesh Gokhale | Abhay Karandikar | Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (BRIC-inStem)

Wonderful to see NITI Aayog feature C-CAMP startup, Biomoneta, for it's stellar innovation  — an air decontamination tech that eliminates >99.99% of airborne pathogens in hospital settings!

Read more:
🔗https://lnkd.in/gCK6CvZC

Biomoneta's Avata Air is an advanced indoor air-purification and microbial decontamination device. Built on their patented ZeBox technology, which uses a non-ionising electric field and a microbicidal surface to capture and destroy 99.99% of airborne microorganisms, including multidrug-resistant bacteria, viruses, and fungi. 

This tech helps create safer spaces in hospitals, including ICUs, operating theatres, IVF facilities, and neonatal care, as well as homes, public spaces, and stringent BSL facilities.  

Biomoneta has recently launched Avata Air through Panasonic for the Indian market!

Biomoneta is supported by C-CAMP through multiple programmes with Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) | Department of Biotechnology | Atal Innovation Mission Official | IT BT Department, Karnataka | Beyond Next Ventures Inc. | India-DST and is a Department of Health and Social Care (GAMRIF, AMR in Environment), SBI Foundation- funded startup under the C-CAMP-anchored India AMR Innovation Hub #IAIH umbrella.

Congratulation Biomoneta! It is a proud milestone for C-CAMP today!

What does it take for an innovation to actually reach the people it was designed to serve?

Sometimes, the biggest barrier isn't the technology. It's everything that needs to happen around it.

During a field visit, a woman farmer in Hatipur handed over ₹10 to the team behind an initiative that had brought new technologies to her community. It wasn't a payment or charity, but a blessing, a reciprocal gesture of gratitude for the economic independence those innovations had helped create.

For Onkar Pandey, Director at Social Alpha, this is what meaningful impact looks like: solutions that respond to real needs and create value for the communities they are designed to serve.

In the second episode of Voices of Value, we draw on Onkar's more than two decades of experience in the development sector to explore what it takes to move agricultural innovations beyond research institutions and pilot projects and into the hands of farmers.

Our conversation looks at why promising technologies often struggle to scale, the role of financing, distribution and after-sales support, and how collaboration between farmers, governments and philanthropic institutions can help build the ecosystems needed for adoption.

Onkar also shares a simple but important piece of advice for early-stage social entrepreneurs:

“Solve the problem. Revenue will chase you.”

A perspective that puts the focus where it belongs: on understanding the problem, earning the trust of communities and building solutions that can sustain themselves over time.

For millions of smallholder farmers, climate change is not an abstract environmental challenge to debate at yet another conference or articulate in yet another report. It is an everyday economic reality. 

Unpredictable rainfall, water scarcity, declining soil health, rising input costs and uncertain crop yields directly affect household incomes and livelihood security. Women face additional disadvantages when technologies, productive assets and market opportunities are not designed around their needs.

These challenges are deeply interconnected. And so must be the solutions. 

This Lab to Land documentary series features six innovators working across soil health, water conservation, biological inputs, clean energy, agricultural mechanisation and sustainable farming. Each innovation approaches a different problem. But together, they illustrate something much larger.

𝗚𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘄𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗻 𝗴𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀, 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀.

And resilience is not simply the ability to survive the next shock. It is the capacity to become progressively less vulnerable while building greater economic opportunity. 

Entrepreneurship is about doing — taking risks, building solutions and demonstrating value. It can play a transformative role in building economic resilience, helping people improve their incomes, reduce costs, manage risks, adapt to climate change and build more secure livelihoods. But a technology must work reliably, demonstrate economic value, become affordable and accessible, and earn the trust of its users. For resource-constrained communities, experimenting with unproven technologies can be prohibitively risky. Someone must absorb those risks, validate solutions and help build the markets that make widespread adoption possible.

Our role is not simply to finance innovation. It is to help create the conditions in which innovation can succeed, markets can emerge, and impact can endure.

These six stories illustrate a larger proposition: economic prosperity, climate resilience, environmental sustainability and social inclusion need not be competing objectives. With the right innovations and institutions, they can reinforce one another.

📢 A Primer on Design Registrations in India | ANRF+ Venture Center Outreach Initiative

How can innovators protect the visual appearance of their products? Understanding design registration is an important step towards safeguarding innovation.

Under the ANRF+ Venture Center Outreach Initiative, we hosted an insightful session on “A Primer on Design Registrations in India”, featuring Archana Joshi, Registered Patent and Trademark Agent, IP & Agreement Services, TechEx.in, Venture Center.

The session helped participants understand the fundamentals of design registration in India, its importance in protecting the visual features of products, and the process of securing design protection.

The session also featured an interactive Ask Me Anything (AMA) with Dr. Premnath V, Director, Venture Center, providing participants an opportunity to engage directly with the experts and clarify their questions on intellectual property protection.

You have validated your business idea. What would help you take the next step?

For women entrepreneurs, that could mean getting registrations in place, understanding finance, reaching new customers or taking the business online.

VentureStudio at Ahmedabad University is partnering with GUSEC as the implementation partner for the Women Acceleration Programme under RAMP, under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, and the Government of Gujarat.

The six-month programme offers selected eligible women-led micro and small enterprises support with:
- Business formalisation and registrations
- Financial readiness and credit linkages
- Digital commerce and market access
- Expert mentoring and business growth planning

The acceleration support is fully covered for selected eligible participants.

Strengthening Gujarat’s innovation ecosystem through collaboration and strategic partnerships.

At the Gujarat Innovation and Technopreneurship (GInTech) Conclave 2026, organised by Savli Technology and Business Incubator (STBI), under the Department of Science & Technology, Government of Gujarat, at GIFT City Club, Gandhinagar, Avinash Punekar, CEO, iCreate, joined government representatives, industry leaders and startup ecosystem stakeholders to discuss advancing technology-led entrepreneurship.

The discussions highlighted the role of incubation, acceleration, industry partnerships, market access and institutional collaboration in helping startups progress from proof-of-concept to scalable enterprises.

The conclave also marked the launch of STBI’s GROWTH Fund, aimed at supporting startup commercialisation and growth.
